subject: Post-demo: GDPR intake, DPA draft request & SCC module preference
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Kapoor <aisha.k@payflow.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Aug 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: GDPR intake, DPA draft request & SCC module preference

Hi Aisha —

Great to meet today and appreciate the clear context on Payflow's use cases (real-time payout routing + anonymized analytics). Quick recap and suggested next steps on the privacy/compliance front so your legal and security teams have everything to move forward:

1) GDPR/DPA & controller/processor role
- Based on the demo and how data flows (you retain customer identifiers and decide routing logic), we recommend Redwood be onboarded as a "processor" for the core inference calls.
- We'll provide a short DPA draft that lists default clauses and the data processing particulars; please confirm if your legal needs a customer-specific clause set.

2) SCC module selection
- Attached is a lightweight SCC module matrix (scc-module-matrix.xlsx) showing typical choices. Our recommendation at this stage is the "SCC Module: Processor - Standard" (Module P-Std) unless Payflow requires a different liability allocation.

3) SOC 2 / Security posture
- We are SOC 2 Type II in-scope (report available under NDA). I'll surface the SOC 2 schedule and a high-level security summary in the DPA package.

4) Vendor security questionnaire
- I've attached our standard vendor security questionnaire (vendor-sec-q.pdf). If Payflow has its own questionnaire, happy to complete it — otherwise we can start with ours and align.

Next steps (proposed timeline):
- Today: I’ll circulate a short DPA draft + SCC module recommendation (attached: redwood_dpa_options.pdf).
- By EOD tomorrow: Ben will start the vendor sec questionnaire response; Ben, can you pick this up?
- Early next week: Vivek can hop on a short call with Payflow security for any technical clarifications.

Aisha — could you confirm the right legal contact for the DPA and whether Payflow has a preferred SCC module or clause to start from? Once we know that, I’ll route the DPA draft for signature (DocuSign link) and attach the SOC 2 NDA if needed.

Thanks again — looking forward to moving this along.

Best,

Lauren Bishop
Senior Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference
lauren@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0183

Attachments: redwood_dpa_options.pdf (summary of DPA options), scc-module-matrix.xlsx, vendor-sec-q.pdf
From: Aisha Kapoor <aisha.k@payflow.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reed <tom.reed@payflow.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Aug 2026 14:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: GDPR intake, DPA draft request & SCC module preference

Thanks Lauren — great demo and very helpful summary.

A few quick clarifying questions from our side before we loop in Legal:
1) Can you confirm the fields Redwood would persist (if any) vs. transient-only inference processing? We need that spelled out for our controller/processor mapping.
2) For SCC Module: our initial preference is to see the recommended language for Processor obligations and liability caps.
3) SOC 2: can you share the scope (Which systems & cutoff dates) and indicate whether there are recent remediation items we should be aware of?

We have our Procurement contact and Legal available: Tom Reed (cc'd) will be the main legal reviewer. He may also ask for a completed vendor security questionnaire — I’ve attached our internal questionnaire (Payflow_Vendor_Sec_Q.xlsx). Can Redwood complete the provided file?

Timeline: If Redwood can return the DPA draft + completed questionnaire by EOD Friday (our timezone), that would map well to our internal procurement sprint next week.

Appreciate it —
Aisha
Head of Platform Partnerships | Payflow Inc
aisha.k@payflow.com | +1 (212) 555-9921

Attachment: Payflow_Vendor_Sec_Q.xlsx

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Aug 2026 08:02:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Post-demo: GDPR intake, DPA draft request & SCC module preference

Looping in Vivek as requested — I started populating Payflow's questionnaire (attached). Notes below for the DPA draft:

- Processing details: Redwood will process inference inputs transiently by default. We do persist KV cache entries for performance which may include non-identifiable tokens; those are configurable and can be disabled if Payflow requests. We will call out persistence behavior explicitly in section 2.1 of the DPA.
- Controller/processor language: Confirming recommendation that Payflow is controller and Redwood is processor. We should include a clause that Payflow controls deletion requests and data subject requests (we'll execute through API or support SLA).
- SCC: Recommend Module P-Std as Lauren suggested. If Payflow prefers a different module we can map the matrix to their requested terms.
- SOC 2: scope includes serving runtime, build/release pipeline for inference infra, and platform control plane (report period Jan 1 - Dec 31, 2025). No open high-severity remediation items; a small medium item related to rotation automation was closed in June 2026. We can share the SOC 2 redacted report under NDA.

Next actions:
- I’ll finish the Payflow_Vendor_Sec_Q.xlsx responses and drop in a shared drive link by EOD (attached: completed_payflow_q.xlsx).
- Lauren: I’ve drafted language for the DPA (section callouts) and will hand it to you for final sign-off before sending to Payflow Legal.

Ben
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Attachments: completed_payflow_q.xlsx

Thanks all — appreciate the quick turnaround and the detail.

Tom (cc): we’d like to move forward with Redwood as a processor. Please review the DPA draft when Lauren shares — we prefer SCC "Module P-Std" as outlined in the matrix, but will confirm if Legal requests any changes.

Ben — thanks for filling out the questionnaire; we received the completed_payflow_q.xlsx and it looks mostly complete. A couple of follow-ups may come from our security team but nothing blocking.

Next items:
- Lauren: please send the DPA draft + DocuSign route and include the SOC 2 NDA so we can review the report.
- Tom: I’ll coordinate Payflow Legal review; target to return redlines within 3 business days.

If helpful I’m available for a short 30-min call Monday morning (your timezone) to close any last items.

Best,
Aisha
Head of Platform Partnerships | Payflow Inc
aisha.k@payflow.com | +1 (212) 555-9921
